name: Wisconsin

regulator.name: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS)

law.name: Uniform Athlete Agents Act, amended to RUAAA in 2019 (Wis. Stat. ch. 440 subch. XIV)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. The act covers endorsement contracts, and since 2019 it also covers paid advisors and business managers (Wis. Stat. 440.99). It does not use the words name, image or likeness.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete. If you sign this contract: 1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; 2) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after signing this contract or before the next scheduled athletic event in which you may participate, whichever occurs first, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and 3) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility as a student athlete in your sport.
summary: Register online with DSPS. $38. Renews June 30 of even years.

steps.detail: Athlete Agent Registration. If you are already registered in another state, use Form 3668 instead.
Pay with the application. DSPS lists the fee in its Renewal Dates and Fees sheet.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: This includes reaching out through someone else. If the athlete reached out first, tell the athletic director within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a signed, written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Say you are registered in Wisconsin and list other states where you are registered. Add your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses and services.

steps.text: Put the warning to student athlete in the contract in bold
steps.detail: Use the state's wording. It must be easy to see.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: A parent or guardian signs too if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy of the contract and the signed warning when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, if that comes first. The athlete must tell the athletic director too.

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel within 14 days of signing
steps.detail: They don't owe you anything if they cancel. They can't give up this right.

steps.text: If the athlete enrolls at a school later, tell its athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: If you knew the athlete before they enrolled and they get an athletic scholarship, tell the school within 10 days of enrolling.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Federal law (SPARTA) bans pre-dating or post-dating it. Put the contract length in too.
Names and addresses, contracts and recruiting costs. DSPS can inspect them and ask for copies.

steps.text: Don't give gifts that could cost the athlete eligibility
steps.detail: If you do, tell the athletic director within 72 hours. The athlete must also sign a note saying they know the risk.

steps.text: Never lie or make false promises to get an athlete to sign
steps.detail: Don't contact athletes to recruit them until you're registered. Federal law (SPARTA) has similar rules.
Every even year. The next renewal is June 30, 2028. No classes required.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.
